annotations.title: Roof Pitch, Slope Factor and Area (Squares of Shingles)

description: Work out roof area from the pitch and the plan (footprint) area. Send one or more roof sections, each with its rise and run (for example rise 6, run 12 for a 6/12 pitch; any units, the same for both) and its plan area in square feet (measured flat, from above, overhangs included) or its plan length and width in feet, plus an optional count. Get back each section's pitch in x/12, slope percent, angle, slope factor, roof area and squares (1 square = 100 sq ft), the totals, the totals with your waste percent, and the shingle bundles to buy at your bundles per square (default 3), rounded up. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/roof-pitch-area). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

bundles_per_square.description: Bundles that cover one square for your shingle (default 3, the common asphalt shingle packing; check the wrapper).

label.description: Optional job label (your own text, echoed; not an address or a person).

sections.description: Roof sections (up to 50). Each: rise, run (default 12), and plan_area or plan_length + plan_width; optional count.

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'south face' (your own text, echoed).

plan_area.description: Plan (horizontal, seen from above) area of this section in square feet, overhangs included.

plan_length.description: Plan length in feet (instead of plan_area).

plan_width.description: Plan width in feet (instead of plan_area).

rise.description: Vertical rise per run (6 for a 6/12 roof). 0 = flat.

run.description: Horizontal run in the same units as rise (default 12).

waste_percent.description: Extra for cutting, starter, hips, ridges and valleys, in percent (default 0).
